title: Offline native artifact admission
scenario: Evaluation-accounting workflow. Use Python 3.11+ and private frozen inputs. Screenshots are browser-rendered actual CLI summaries with fake native journals, qualification and usage; not terminal images or real inference.

steps.title: Submit recorded artifact evidence
steps.instruction: Prepare the private input according to the evaluation-accounting guide. Run trial_admission.py report with JSON stdin and retain the report. Inspect every scheduled trial; exit 0 means a report was produced, not that every trial passed.
steps.caption: Actual collector and reader CLI smoke: synthetic lifecycle evidence. Runtime source bytes match checkpoint fa2ae1202398; execution preceded the commit and was matched afterwards.
steps.expected: One pass, two fails and one unsubmitted inconclusive. Synthetic usage is 480 known tokens; total unknown and live_eligible false. Current real qualification remains blocked.

steps.title: Keep duplicates and refusals visible
steps.instruction: Retain failed and duplicate submissions. In an owned synthetic fixture, submit the same attempt twice and verify one cumulative usage charge. Check that a caller qualification flag is rejected and only the owned disposable fixture is removed.
steps.caption: Actual separate CLI results from fake journals: two submissions, one source attempt; arbitrary qualification flag rejected. This is no authentication or model proof.
steps.expected: Duplicate coverage and missing trials remain visible. Synthetic 160 known tokens are a subtotal; total unknown. Explicit model export and launch reservations remain separate requirements.
